title.narrative: Eighth Global Environment Facility Replenishment - Core Contribution - Environmental Challenges

description.narrative: The Global Environment Facility (GEF) was established in 1992 and is a multilateral family of funds dedicated to addressing climate change, biodiversity loss, pollution, and supporting land and ocean health. Through the GEF, Australia meets its financial obligations under numerous multilateral environmental agreements to support developing countries address environmental challenges, including the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity, United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification, Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants and Minamata Convention on Mercury. This funding (total value: $80 million) represents Australia's contribution to the GEF's eighth replenishment (2022-26). Funding is provided to the GEF Trust Fund with the World Bank as trustee.

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

description.narrative: Through the Global Environment Facility (GEF), Australia supports developing countries to address climate change, biodiversity loss, pollution, and to support land and ocean health through six multilateral environmental agreements, including the United Nations (UN) Framework Convention on Climate Change, the UN Convention on Biological Diversity, the UN Convention to Combat Desertification, Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants, Minamata Convention on Mercury and Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction Agreement. A longstanding supporter of the GEF, Australia currently contributes to the GEF’s Eighth Replenishment (2022-2026) and is GEF Council Co-Chair in 2025. Australia promotes strong governance and increased access for our Pacific partners, as well as small island developing states and least developed countries globally. DFAT’s funding to the GEF is estimated to have supported 205,222 smallholder farmers to improve food security and 191,331 smallholder farmers for climate resilient agriculture.
